geography.name: Morris County, New Jersey
geography.scopeNote: County labor/CBP, county-wide ACS tracts, and a separately selected multi-county Chamber directory footprint.

coverage.vintagePolicy: Observed input values only; modeled results and hypothetical scenarios explicitly typed. Data are latest-vintage snapshots acquired at source-specific times, not reconstructed real-time vintages.
warnings: Never interpret these outputs as local GDP growth.
ACS is a pooled 2020-2024 sample; CBP comparison window is 2018-2023; LAUS has its own monthly availability.
October 2025 county LAUS is missing in BLS because of the lapse in appropriations.
Existing Chamber categories are directory labels, not verified NAICS classifications.

forecast.title: County unemployment forecast

method.name: Rolling-origin benchmark selection
method.description: Seasonal-naive and local-level seasonal state-space forecasts compete on purged selection folds; final ten origins are held out.

limitations: Target is county resident unemployment rate, not Mount Olive GDP or commercial activity.
Latest-vintage backtests are not real-time-vintage backtests; revisions may improve retrospective results.
Overlapping forecast horizons create dependent errors; aggregate metrics have no claimed standard errors.
90% intervals are nominal and do not include parameter uncertainty or future structural breaks.
The selected state-space model underperforms seasonal naive on the final holdout; broad intervals over-cover this small evaluation sample. Predictive superiority is not established.
Missing October 2025 is retained. Kalman filtering skips its observation update; validation never scores it.
Seasonal-naive baseline uses the last observed same-calendar-month value if the previous year is missing.
Selected model is chosen using 1-3 month validation; months 4-6 are extrapolations without matching-horizon validation.

validation.design: 30 rolling origins; 1-3 month horizons; rolling 120-month training; final 10 origins held out; overlapping selection targets purged
validation.vintagePolicy: Pseudo out-of-sample, latest-vintage observations. Release-time revisions are not reconstructed.
validation.selectionRule: Lowest selection MAE among models completing every selection fold; no holdout-based selection

diagnostics.model: Gaussian local level + deterministic 12-month seasonal state

holdoutAssessment.note: Selection is frozen before holdout. A worse holdout score is retained and reported, not used to reselect.

nowcast.title: Current-month county labor projection

method.name: Kalman state-space projection to current month
method.description: Projects lagged official county unemployment data to the current month; no contemporaneous external signals are available.

requirements.name: Higher-frequency contemporaneous signals
requirements.detail: No permits, traffic, sales or search feed

limitations: Target is county resident unemployment rate, not Mount Olive GDP or commercial activity.
Latest-vintage backtests are not real-time-vintage backtests; revisions may improve retrospective results.
Overlapping forecast horizons create dependent errors; aggregate metrics have no claimed standard errors.
90% intervals are nominal and do not include parameter uncertainty or future structural breaks.
The selected state-space model underperforms seasonal naive on the final holdout; broad intervals over-cover this small evaluation sample. Predictive superiority is not established.
Missing October 2025 is retained. Kalman filtering skips its observation update; validation never scores it.
Seasonal-naive baseline uses the last observed same-calendar-month value if the previous year is missing.
Selected model is chosen using 1-3 month validation; months 4-6 are extrapolations without matching-horizon validation.
This is a univariate current-month projection, not a mixed-frequency nowcast.

result.informationSet: Published county LAUS observations only; no current-month covariates

stateSpaceModel.model: Gaussian local level + deterministic 12-month seasonal state

anomalies.title: County labor early-warning screen

method.name: Past-only seasonal residual MAD and empirical-tail screening
method.description: Robust residual scores use only prior seasonal differences; empirical tail ranks receive BH correction within the displayed family.

limitations: Robust score magnitude is a screening statistic, not a calibrated Gaussian z-score.
Empirical p-values require exchangeability; serial dependence and regime changes weaken that approximation.
No alert is a recession classification or a prediction of business closure.
Absence of a flag does not establish economic stability; finite calibration samples limit p-value resolution.

result.interpretation: Red alerts require BH q<=0.05; |MAD score|>=3 is a separate unconfirmed screening flag.

health.title: Household socioeconomic context

method.name: Standardized PCA with spatial-block loading stability
method.description: An exploratory cross-sectional composite, oriented toward higher income. Scores are relative to included county tracts.

requirements.name: External commercial-health validation
requirements.detail: No vacancies, openings, closure or sales outcome panel

requirements.name: Coherent favorable component loadings
requirements.detail: Mixed signs imply an income/workforce-composition contrast, not an ordered health scale

limitations: This is not a validated local economic health score; overallEconomicHealthScore remains null.
Income and poverty are correlated; explained variance is not evidence of economic validity.
Employment ratio is influenced by age composition and retirement, not just labor demand.
The observed component loads negatively on employment/population; higher scores cannot be interpreted as uniformly healthier.
No score confidence interval: cross-variable ACS sampling covariances are unavailable.
Tracts with missing, top-coded income >=250000, or income MOE/estimate >=0.5 are excluded.
Spatial-block bootstrap is a descriptive stability diagnostic, not calibrated inferential uncertainty.

result.interpretation: Relative ACS 2020-2024 tract context; mean 50, SD 10; not bounded to 0-100
result.validation: 250 resamples of eight geographic KMeans blocks; sign-invariant loading cosine. No predictive outcome validation.

spatial.title: Spatial income association

method.name: Global and conditional Local Moran permutation tests
method.description: Tests spatial association in observed tract median household income, with two-sided randomization tests and BH-adjusted local p-values.

limitations: Income clustering is residential context, not a business hotspot or a causal spillover.
Graph uses interior representative points, not contiguity or road travel times.
Permutation p-values condition on estimates; ACS survey error is not part of the null test.
Independent normal MOE perturbations are sensitivity analysis only; survey covariance is unknown.
BH local correction assumes an appropriate dependence structure; shared-neighbor tests remain exploratory.
Missing and top-coded median incomes are excluded, potentially changing the graph.

result.weightDefinition: Union-symmetrized 6 nearest neighbors by haversine distance, then row-standardized; diagonal zero

measurementError.label: MOE sensitivity range, not a confidence interval

network.title: Industry specialization and relation networks

method.name: RCA, co-specialization graph, diversification and centrality
method.description: Compares observed county industry establishment shares to a New Jersey reference and measures graph structure.

limitations: CBP excludes nonemployers and many public-sector activities; establishments are not firms.
Shares and RCA use only sectors published for every included county; coverage is reported explicitly.
Industry similarity and directory relations do not identify economic anchors or causal supply links.
County differences may reflect land use, size and demographics; no causal interpretation.
Annual employment is a March reference-week count; payroll is nominal, not inflation-adjusted.
2018-2023 is the fixed comparison window; no claim that 2023 is the newest release.

result.referenceGeography: New Jersey counties, complete published sectors

sectorCoverage.exclusionReason: Not published for every NJ county; missing source records are not assumed zero

result.edgeMeaning: Co-specialization proximity: min[P(RCA_i>=1|RCA_j>=1), P(RCA_j>=1|RCA_i>=1)] across NJ counties; edges >=0.55. Association only, no supplier/customer claims.
result.complexityReadiness: ECI ranking withheld: 21 county rows and broad sectors are a fragile economic-complexity basis; report RCA and diversification descriptively.

resilience.title: Conditional industry exposure stress test

method.name: Linear network sensitivity under explicit assumed coupling
method.description: Uses observed establishment shares as exposure weights and hypothetical coupling over an association graph.

requirements.name: Estimated transmission coefficients
requirements.detail: Coupling 0, 0.15 and 0.30 are analyst illustration assumptions

limitations: Outputs are conditional exposure units, not predicted closures, employment loss, dollar impact, or GDP.
Association-graph edges are not economic transmission evidence; zero coupling is the direct-only baseline.
A linear response can overstate large shocks; these are small-shock sensitivity illustrations.

result.basis: Observed employer establishment shares in included sectors
assumptions: Illustrative 20% sector activity stress, not an estimated event probability
Equivalent-establishment units normalize exposure; they are not predicted actual closures

policy.title: Policy allocation assumptions

method.name: User-specified binary resource allocation
method.library: Browser javascript-lp-solver maintained by main application
method.formula: max sum_j assumed_benefit_j x_j, subject to cost, equity and risk constraints; x_j in {0,1}
method.description: The live browser policy lab solves explicit user scenarios. Python does not supply estimated causal benefits.

requirements.name: User costs, benefit assumptions and constraints
requirements.detail: Configured in the browser policy lab

limitations: An optimizer chooses under its inputs; it does not validate intervention effectiveness.
No synthetic proposal benefits are written into observed model results.

survival.title: Business survival readiness

method.name: Kaplan-Meier with optional delayed entry
method.description: Reusable right-censored survival estimator is implemented and tested on synthetic fixtures only.

requirements.name: Business opening and verified closure dates
requirements.detail: Directory presence is not survival history

requirements.name: Censoring dates and delayed-entry records
requirements.detail: Must distinguish closure from missing or unlisted

limitations: No observed survival estimates are published.
Independent censoring is required; membership renewal dates cannot substitute for business closure.
Cox and competing-risk models need more covariates and events than this snapshot provides.

causal.title: Causal policy evaluation readiness

method.name: Common-adoption panel difference-in-differences
method.description: Reusable balanced-panel estimator with common treatment timing, unit/time effects and clustered uncertainty; tested on synthetic fixtures only.

requirements.name: Defined intervention and adoption date
requirements.detail: No identified intervention in observed data

requirements.name: Measured outcome and comparison panel
requirements.detail: At least 3 pre and 2 post periods; 10 treated and 10 control units enforced

requirements.name: Defensible identification
requirements.detail: Parallel trends, no anticipation, no interference, stable composition

limitations: No causal effect is estimated from the current snapshot.
Parallel trends is an assumption, not established by a nonsignificant pretrend test.
Staggered adoption is rejected; this estimator is not a general heterogeneous-treatment TWFE solution.
Twenty clusters is a minimum guard, not assurance of calibrated inference; small-cluster bootstrap may be needed.
